newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Monkey cosmonaut dies of heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Monkey cosmonaut dies of heart attack.

text.p: Multik, one of two Russian monkeys just back from a two-week space mission, died of a heart attack after post-flight tests but scientists insisted on Thursday that the mishap had nothing to do with the mission.
"There was an unfortunate incident," Itar-Tass news agency quoted the deputy head of Moscow's Medico-Biological Institute, Yevgeny Ilyin, as saying.
"This is the first such instance in our experience. It was an unfortunate incident which couldn't have been foreseen."

Ilyin said Multik and his flight partner Lapik, both male, came down safely on Tuesday in their Bion-11 research capsule after hurtling round the Earth for a fortnight in a U.S.-funded mission criticised by animal rights groups.
Tests of the two monkeys' coordination on Wednesday went well, but Multik's heart stopped after bone and muscle samples were taken under general anaesthetic.

Tass said a team of doctors from Russia, the United States and France were unable to revive the monkey. Ilyin said the flight had up until then proved a huge success in helping to understand the effect of weightlessness on humans.
The U.S. space agency NASA put up half the cost of the $30-million mission, during which the monkeys' brains were wired up to electrodes as part of research into weightlessness.
Animal rights groups in the United States protested against the experiment, the latest in a research programme begun by the Soviet Union in 1973. The next Bion flight is due next year.
France, Ukraine and Lithuania also took part in Bion-11.
